children: Foreign selling of Gulf equities accelerated in August even as regional stock markets rallied, Iridium Advisors says. Net foreign outflows widened to $544 million from $415 million in July, led by $351 million from the U.A.E. and $202 million from Saudi Arabia. Qatar bucked the trend with a $62 million inflow, its first since February. The divergence comes as the MSCI GCC Index gained 3.9% in August, outperforming emerging markets for a second consecutive month, suggesting local market strength hasn't yet translated into a broad return of foreign capital. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
